match.reason: The closest bank point covers habitat clearing, removing species and introduced species such as the cane toad, but it does not teach climate change or seasonal migration, which the new point needs, so adding them would be a new step rather than a small adjustment.

draft.title: Changes to populations
card: A population is all the members of one species living in an area. Its size can rise or fall when something changes in the ecosystem.
Habitat loss and climate change
Clearing land removes the food and shelter a species needs, so its population can fall. A changing climate can alter temperature and rainfall, which can also shrink or grow populations.
Migration
Some animals move away for part of each year, such as birds that fly to another region for the warmer months. The population in the area they leave falls for that time and rises when they return.
Adding or removing a species

Because species are linked in a food web, one change spreads. Cane toads were brought to Australia and poison many animals that eat them, so some predator populations fell. Foxes eat small native animals, so their populations can fall where foxes live.
draft.remember: A change to one part of a food web, such as habitat, climate, migration or a new species, can change population sizes.

a.q: A forest is cleared for farmland. Why might the population of a small bird that nests there fall?
opts: It loses the shelter and food it needs
It starts to migrate for part of each year
Its predators are removed from the forest
It is poisoned by a newly added species
a.why: Clearing the forest is habitat loss, which removes the food and shelter the bird needs, so fewer birds can survive. Migration is a seasonal move, not a result of clearing land, so it is not the reason here.
a.clue: Think about what the bird gets from the forest.

b.q: A fox is brought to an island where small ground-nesting birds are the main food of a native cat. Foxes also eat the birds. What is the most likely effect on the native cat population?
opts: It falls, as the birds it eats become fewer
It rises, as the foxes give it extra food
It stays the same, as foxes are not related
It rises, as the birds become more numerous
b.why: Foxes eat the birds, so the bird population is likely to fall. The native cat then has less food, so its population is likely to fall too. The change spreads through the food web even though foxes and cats do not interact directly.
b.clue: Follow the change from the fox to the birds, then to the cat.

a.best: It loses the shelter and food it needs

b.best: It falls, as the birds it eats become fewer

problems.detail: The remember line calls habitat, climate and migration 'part of a food web'. Habitat and climate are not parts of a food web. The card says more accurately that something changes 'in the ecosystem'. Suggest 'A change in an ecosystem, such as...'.

Why (b) says foxes and cats 'do not interact directly'. The card does not teach this, and foxes and native cats can compete or fight directly. Better to say only that the change reaches the cat through its food supply.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer and the card's facts are correct. The remember line wrongly calls habitat and climate parts of a food web, and why (b) adds an untaught claim that foxes and cats do not interact directly.
